questions.stem: A sample of nitrogen gas, N₂, has a mass of $14$ g. Calculate the amount of nitrogen in moles, and the volume this amount occupies at room temperature and pressure. ($M_r$(N₂) $= 28$; molar gas volume at r.t.p. $= 24\text{ dm}^3$)
questions.modelAnswer: Moles of nitrogen $= \dfrac{14}{28} = 0.50$ mol. One mole of any gas fills $24\text{ dm}^3$ at r.t.p., so $0.50$ mol fills $0.50 \times 24 = 12\text{ dm}^3$.

questions.stem: $20.0\text{ cm}^3$ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration $0.150\text{ mol/dm}^3$ is exactly neutralised by $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of dilute sulfuric acid. The equation is 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in $\text{mol/dm}^3$.
questions.modelAnswer: Convert volumes to dm³ and find the moles of alkali: $0.0200 \times 0.150 = 0.00300$ mol. The equation shows two moles of NaOH neutralise one mole of H₂SO₄, so the acid amount is $\dfrac{0.00300}{2} = 0.00150$ mol. That amount sat in $0.0250\text{ dm}^3$, giving $c = \dfrac{0.00150}{0.0250} = 0.0600\text{ mol/dm}^3$.

questions.stem: For the reaction 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, use the bond energies H–H $= 436$, O=O $= 496$ and O–H $= 463\text{ kJ/mol}$ to calculate the enthalpy change $\Delta H$, and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
markscheme: M1: energy taken in to break bonds $= 2 \times 436 + 496 = 1368\text{ kJ/mol}$
M1: energy released forming bonds $= 4 \times 463 = 1852\text{ kJ/mol}$
A1: $\Delta H = 1368 - 1852 = -484\text{ kJ/mol}$; negative, so exothermic
questions.modelAnswer: Breaking $2$ H–H bonds and $1$ O=O bond absorbs $2 \times 436 + 496 = 1368\text{ kJ/mol}$. Forming the $4$ O–H bonds in two water molecules releases $4 \times 463 = 1852\text{ kJ/mol}$. $\Delta H = 1368 - 1852 = -484\text{ kJ/mol}$ — forming the new bonds pays out more energy than breaking the old ones costs, so heat is given out: exothermic.

questions.stem: In the Haber process, ammonia is made from the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), which is exothermic in the forward direction. Explain why the industrial process uses a high pressure, and why a temperature of about $450\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ is chosen rather than a much lower one.
markscheme: B1: four moles of gas react to give two, so raising the pressure pushes the equilibrium towards ammonia
B1: a low temperature would favour the yield but would make the reaction too slow
B1: $450\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ is a compromise — acceptable yield at a commercially viable rate
questions.modelAnswer: The forward change converts 4 moles of gas into 2, so compressing the mixture drives the equilibrium towards the ammonia side. Cooling would improve the equilibrium yield because the forward reaction releases heat, but at a low temperature the particles collide too slowly for economical production. Around $450\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ balances a decent yield against a fast enough rate, with the iron catalyst keeping the rate high at that temperature.

questions.stem: A solution containing Fe²⁺ ions is added to acidified potassium manganate(VII) solution. State the colour change observed, and explain the role of the Fe²⁺ ions in terms of electron transfer.
markscheme: B1: the purple manganate(VII) solution turns colourless
B1: Fe²⁺ acts as the reducing agent — it loses electrons (Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺) and is itself oxidised
questions.modelAnswer: The deep purple colour of the manganate(VII) disappears as MnO₄⁻ is reduced. Each Fe²⁺ ion donates an electron to become Fe³⁺, so Fe²⁺ is the reducing agent and is oxidised in the process.

questions.stem: But-1-ene and but-2-ene are both alkenes with the molecular formula C₄H₈. Explain why they are described as isomers.
markscheme: B1: they share the same molecular formula (C₄H₈)
B1: but their structures differ — the C=C double bond sits between different carbon atoms
questions.modelAnswer: Both molecules contain four carbons and eight hydrogens, giving the identical molecular formula C₄H₈. In but-1-ene the double bond joins carbons 1 and 2, while in but-2-ene it joins carbons 2 and 3 — a different arrangement of the same atoms, which is exactly what isomers are.

questions.stem: During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride, chlorine gas forms at the anode. Write the ionic half-equation for this anode reaction.
markscheme: M1: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ (species correct)
A1: equation balanced for both atoms and charge
questions.modelAnswer: Two chloride ions each give up one electron to form a chlorine molecule: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. The equation balances with two chlorines and a charge of −2 on each side.

questions.stem: Nylon is made by condensation polymerisation, whereas poly(ethene) is made by addition polymerisation. Describe two differences between these types of polymerisation.
markscheme: B1: addition polymerisation uses one monomer containing a C=C double bond; condensation uses monomers with two reactive functional groups
B1: condensation releases a small molecule (such as water) every time a link forms; addition produces no by-product
B1: addition polymers have a backbone of carbon atoms only, while condensation polymers (nylon, PET) contain amide or ester links in the chain
questions.modelAnswer: In addition polymerisation, many copies of a single unsaturated monomer such as ethene join across their double bonds, and nothing else is produced. In condensation polymerisation, monomers carrying two functional groups react and each new link expels a small molecule such as water. The chains differ too: poly(ethene) is all carbon down the backbone, whereas nylon and PET carry amide or ester linkages along the chain.
